rationale: Ground truth is a light 'LGTM' approval with 4 minor style/organization comments (unrelated-hunk question, all2all kwargs-vs-explicit style, two move-to-utils asks); neither candidate explicitly surfaces any of these, so recall is low for both. X's review hinges on a dramatic, hard-to-verify 'reproduced' claim of a scheduler double-seeding bug and recommends blocking an already-approved, merged PR — a high-risk headline finding unsupported by the actual review/CI outcome and the PR's own targeted test suite for that exact scenario. Y's findings (headless compile-cache isolation gaps, dead async_tokens_to_discard writes — independently corroborated by X, lending it credibility) are more measured and verifiable via static reasoning, and its 'approve with follow-ups' verdict better matches the PR's real approved/merged status. Both reviews are comparably concrete and actionable with specific file/line citations and proposed fixes.
